leaves.says: A player cannot research and build an ancient machine, and nothing in the world gives the colony a working one: the colony gets a working one only when its colonists repair a wreck.

meant.intent: Reject if false: if a colony can build an ancient machine from the menu or buy a working one, the wreck and its repair are a detour and the mod has no promise left. His statement: the machines 'can no longer simply be researched and built like normal', and the Original is 'no longer attainable through research or repair, used only for comparison'. An ancient machine is each production machine of the factory mod, the vanometric power cell and the psychic emanator, while its line in Mod Settings is on.
meant.source: OWNER:1795755622961436106 (his statement of the mod); OWNER:1795761534460592124 (by card: all 18 machines); OWNER:1795749543738184808 ('remove the VFE factory, not the manual one'); delegated: record decisions d_no_working_original_in_the_world (the Designer's reading of 'used only for comparison', call B of turn 5, CONDUCTOR:1795770570858909459) and d_all_eighteen_shape (the parts that carry goods stay buildable; a machine that stands in an older save is not changed).

figurative.stands_for: the ways the game itself hands things to a colony: loot on a generated map, a quest reward and a trader's stock. It does not mean a machine that already stands in an older save, and it does not mean a development command.
figurative.accept: A colony that loads an older save keeps the working factory machines that already stand in it.

figurative.stands_for: at the Kludged, Refurbished or Original level. A Wrecked machine is the thing a colony does find.
figurative.accept: A ruin room holds a wrecked autoloom, and that find breaks nothing in this bar.

accept: The Factory tab of the build menu lists the conveyors, the hoppers, the factory floor and the other parts that carry goods, and no machine that makes goods. The base game's electric smelter is still in its own tab.

A trader of exotic goods visits and a quest offers its rewards. Neither holds a working vanometric power cell or a working psychic emanator. The colony's first working power cell is the one that its colonists repaired.
A colony finishes every research project in the game. No level of an ancient machine appears in the build menu, the Wrecked level included.
A colony that loads an older save keeps the working factory machines that already stand in it.
reject: The automated smelter is gone from the build menu, and the other factory machines are researched and built as before.
No machine is in the build menu, and a quest reward still hands the colony a working psychic emanator.
The Wrecked level of a machine is in the build menu for a little steel, so a colony builds a wreck beside its base and never has to find one.
Every machine leaves the build menu and every hand-out, and the conveyors, the hoppers and the base game's electric smelter leave with them.
leaves.lazy: Every machine leaves the build menu and every hand-out, and the conveyors, the hoppers and the base game's electric smelter leave with them.

range.varies: Each of the 20 ancient machines: the 18 production machines of the factory mod (17 when Vanilla Cooking Expanded is not loaded; the fish farm's def loads with Odyssey), the vanometric power cell and the psychic emanator. Grouped by how they could fail: the factory machines (build menu and research); the two base-game machines (reward lists, trader stock and map loot of Core, Ideology, Odyssey and Anomaly). Each level of each machine. A new game with no research, and a game with every research project finished.
range.left_out: A machine whose Mod Settings line is off (bar switch_gives_machine_back). The Mod Setting that puts the Original back in the build menu: a player's override that is off as shipped; no bar judges the Original as a thing a colony reaches. A machine that stands in an older save. Development commands. Another mod that hands out a factory machine by a list of its own: not searched for. Whether any trader's stock reads the factory mod's thing category is UNMEASURED today; the reading of this bar settles it.

sees.instrument: A state read in a loaded game. (1) jawa/architect_designator_visible for each level of each ancient machine and for the factory mod's parts. (2) The same read after every research project is finished (jawa/research_bulk). (3) The reward, loot and trader-stock generators that can produce a building, each run many times, and the list of the defs that they produced. Reading (3) needs one generic bridge function that does not exist yet (run a ThingSetMakerDef, or a TraderKindDef's stock, N times and list the defs): a build item of the scene.
sees.start: A loaded game on the mod's small list (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/version/small_list.json), all five expansions, a quicktest map. Every machine's line at its shipped value (asserted by a settings read). No research finished (asserted).
sees.on: Every machine's Mod Settings line on. The full-restoration setting off.
sees.control: The cheapest other explanation is an instrument that cannot see a machine in a menu or in a generator's output. The same reads with one factory machine's line off must show that machine in the build menu, and with the power cell's line off the generators must produce a working power cell at least once.
sees.reset: Put the settings back and read them back; close the quicktest map. Nothing persistent changes.
sees.live_only_why: The mod changes defs at startup in C#, and the generators read the lists of five expansions. Only the loaded game holds those lists as they are.

leaves.experience: A player cannot research and build an ancient machine, and nothing in the world gives the colony a working one: the colony gets a working one only when its colonists repair a wreck.

leaves.says: A player meets wrecked machines in the world: they lie in the rooms of ancient ruins, and now and then one lies half-buried on an ordinary map when the colony arrives.

meant.intent: Reject if false: with no wreck in the world the mod never starts. That is failure mode 1 of the record: 'There is no way in'. His card adds that every colony meets the mod, even one that never leaves home.
meant.source: OWNER:1795755647483442186 (by card: 'Ruins, plus a rare wreck'); OWNER:1795755622961436106 ('they must be found'); OWNER:1795755673273656447 (which machine a colony gets first is 'an Utinni-tier decision independent of this mod'); delegated: record decisions d_found_is_wrecked (a found machine is always at the Wrecked level; which wrecks lie where is a weighted list that a layer above can change) and d_feasible_wreck_placement.

figurative.stands_for: the wreck reads as old and left behind where it lies. It is a plain building on the map. It is not a thing that colonists must dig out.
figurative.accept: A wreck stands in the open among rubble, and a colonist walks up to it and uninstalls it with no digging.

figurative.stands_for: some new maps hold one such wreck and many hold none. How often is a Mod Setting and is never part of this bar.
figurative.accept: A player starts several colonies and only some of the maps hold a wreck.

accept: A colony explores an ancient ruin on its own map and finds a wrecked machine in one of the rooms. The wreck is whole enough to recognise as a machine, and it does no work.
A player starts a colony on an ordinary map with no ruin and sees one wrecked machine among rubble. The map of the player's next colony holds none.
Over many ruins a player finds wrecks of many different machines, large factory machines and carried ones.
A wreck stands in the open among rubble, and a colonist walks up to it and uninstalls it with no digging.
reject: Wrecks lie only in ruins on other world tiles, so a colony that stays at home never sees one.
A machine that a colony finds is already Kludged or Refurbished and works when power reaches it.
Every ruin room and every new map holds wrecks, so a colony collects a full factory in its first season.
Wrecks lie in ruins and on ordinary maps, and each of them is the same one machine.
leaves.lazy: Wrecks lie in ruins and on ordinary maps, and each of them is the same one machine.

range.varies: The sites: an ancient ruin on the colony's own map, an ancient ruin on a visited tile (Odyssey's ancient complexes and the base game's ancient ruins), and an ordinary new map with no ruin. The placement reads no biome: it reads whether a ruin room or open ground exists (GUIDING_PRINCIPLES.md entry 1), so it is tested on the biome of the small list's test map. Which machine: the weighted list of all 20. Map sizes 200 to 325.
range.left_out: How often a wreck appears and which machine is most common: tuning data in Mod Settings and in the placement list. Which machine the campaign gives first: the campaign's own list. A quest that points at a wreck: not in 0.1.0. Any second planet or change to the world: never.

sees.instrument: A count on generated maps in a loaded game. (1) Generate a map that holds an ancient ruin and list this mod's wrecks with their cells (jawa/list_things by defName); each cell must be inside a ruin room. (2) Run the ordinary-map placement on fresh maps with its chance at the shipped value, for a number of maps written before the first run, and count the maps with one wreck and with none. (3) Read the level of each machine found. Reading (2) is random by design, so the tester writes X of Y in the test table before the first run (kind B).
sees.start: A loaded game on the mod's small list (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/version/small_list.json), all five expansions, a quicktest map. A fresh map with no thing of this mod on it before the generation step (asserted). The mod's placement list read back: it holds every ancient machine whose line is on.
sees.on: Every machine's line on. The two placement switches (ruins, ordinary maps) at their shipped values.
sees.control: The cheapest other explanation is a wreck that the scene itself spawned, or a wreck that another mod placed (FlowWorks and Cold Storage place wrecks of their own). The scene spawns nothing and counts only this mod's defs. The same ruin map generated with this mod's ruin placement switched off holds no wreck of this mod.
sees.live_only_why: Placement runs inside the game's map generation, in the ruin rooms that Odyssey makes. No offline copy of that generator exists.

leaves.experience: A player meets wrecked machines in the world: they lie in the rooms of ancient ruins, and now and then one lies half-buried on an ordinary map when the colony arrives.

leaves.says: Colonists can take up any wreck, carry it away and set it down where the colony wants it.

meant.intent: Reject if false: his statement says that a machine is 'found and retrieved to a safe location'. A wreck that cannot leave the ruin can only be repaired where the danger is, and a wreck on another tile is lost to the colony. The built smelter wreck has no carried form today.
meant.source: OWNER:1795755622961436106; OWNER:1795762605668672773 (by card: 'Colonists carry it'); OWNER:1795760440829904733 (hauler droids and ride-in machines: the campaign's narrowing); delegated: record decisions d_wreck_is_carried and d_lift_is_data (who may lift a wreck is data on the machine that a layer above can narrow).

figurative.stands_for: the Wrecked level of each ancient machine, the largest factory machine included. A machine at a repaired level may be fixed in place: that is data of each machine.
figurative.accept: A wrecked smelter as large as a small room is uninstalled, and colonists with a pack animal bring it home from another tile.

figurative.stands_for: on any ground that carries a heavy building. A wreck does not need the factory floor that the working machine needs.
figurative.accept: A colony with no factory research sets a wrecked smelter down on the bare floor of its workshop.

accept: A colonist uninstalls a wrecked smelter in a ruin, hauls it to the colony's workshop and installs it there. It stands as the same wreck.
A caravan loads a wrecked autoloom that it found on another tile. Its weight takes the load of more than one colonist, or of a pack animal. It arrives, and colonists install it at home.
In a game where a mod above this one narrows who may lift a wreck, a colonist has no uninstall order on the wreck and a hauler droid carries it instead.
A colony with no factory research sets a wrecked smelter down on the bare floor of its workshop.
reject: The small wrecks can be carried, and the large factory wrecks have no uninstall order.
A wreck can be uninstalled, and its carried form cannot be set down at home because it needs a floor that the colony has no research to build.
Colonists carry a wreck home, and the thing that they set down is a machine at another level.
leaves.lazy: none: the words name the three acts (take up, carry, set down) and say 'any wreck'. A build that does the three acts for every wreck with the base game's own uninstall and install is the bar. The card names the cost that he accepted: an ancient machine lifts as easily as a loom.

range.varies: Each of the 20 wrecks, grouped by size and weight (the factory wrecks weigh what the factory mod's machines weigh, 35 to 115 kg; the two carried machines). A wreck with no owner in a ruin and a wreck that the colony owns. A move inside one map and a move by caravan from another tile. A colonist and a pack animal. Ground: bare soil, a plain floor, the factory floor.
range.left_out: Who may lift a wreck in the campaign: data that a layer above narrows; this mod does not know that Droidworks exists. Whether a Kludged or Refurbished machine can be moved: rule R_kludged_move. His four words 'but notified or built' are not read, and nothing rests on them. Transport pods and gravships: the base game's, not judged.

sees.instrument: One colonist and one order per wreck group, in a loaded game: the Uninstall order on a wreck that has no owner, a read that the carried form exists and that the colonist carries it, an install order at another cell, and a read that the same Wrecked machine stands there. For the other wrecks a state read of each wreck def's carried form and of its mass against one colonist's carry capacity. The install order needs one generic bridge function that does not exist yet (place the install blueprint of a carried building): a build item of the scene.
sees.start: A loaded game on the mod's small list (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/version/small_list.json), all five expansions, a quicktest map. A wrecked smelter and a wrecked power cell with no faction on open ground. One colonist who can haul, with no job (asserted). A clear install cell on a plain floor some cells away (asserted).
sees.on: The machines' lines on. No mod above this one loaded, so nothing narrows the lift.
sees.control: The cheapest other explanation is a scene that moved the wreck by a command and not by a colonist. The scene reads the colonist's job at each step (uninstall, haul, install). A wall beside the wreck, which has no carried form, must refuse the Uninstall order: the instrument can see a refusal.
sees.reset: Destroy the spawned things; close the quicktest map.
sees.live_only_why: Carrying is a chain of colonist jobs. A def read shows that a carried form exists; it does not show that a colonist finishes the chain with a machine of that size and sets it down.

leaves.experience: Colonists can take up any wreck, carry it away and set it down where the colony wants it.

leaves.says: Colonists study the machine itself, and only that study opens the research for its next repair.

meant.intent: Reject if false: his words make the machine in front of the colonist the subject of the research. If a bench alone opens the repair, the wreck is one more ingredient of a recipe. In the built mod the first repair needs no study and no research, and study exists only with another mod loaded.
meant.source: OWNER:1795755622961436106 ('studied to enable research'; 'Each repair requires machine study, research bench time, and considerable resources'); OWNER:1795749426260848822 ('study the MACHINE itself as part of the research'); OWNER:1795749555968288570 ('It should teach them about how to fix that machine... slowly'); delegated: record decisions d_study_before_each_repair (two projects for each machine; the base game's own study carries it; research is the colony's knowledge) and d_first_look_read reading 3 (no item of another mod; turned on once; progress shown on the machine).

figurative.stands_for: the project for a repair cannot be started at a bench until colonists have studied a machine of that kind at the level below. It does not mean that study replaces the bench.
figurative.accept: After the study is complete, researchers finish the project at an ordinary research bench, away from the machine.

figurative.stands_for: a machine of that kind at that level, standing on the map. What is learned belongs to the colony afterwards.
figurative.accept: A colony that repaired one smelter repairs a second wrecked smelter with no new study.

accept: The player selects a wreck and turns study on once. A colonist who does research walks to the wreck and studies it, comes back to it over the next days without a new order, and the wreck shows how far its study is.

Before the study is complete, the research screen shows the machine's first restoration project as locked and says that the wreck must be studied. When the study is complete, a message says so and the project can be started.
Colonists study the Kludged machine in the same way, and that study opens the second project, the one for the repair to Refurbished.
After the study is complete, researchers finish the project at an ordinary research bench, away from the machine.
A colony that repaired one smelter repairs a second wrecked smelter with no new study.
reject: The restoration project can be researched at a bench from the first day, and study of the wreck only makes it faster.
Study works only when another mod is loaded, or only when the colonist carries a special kit. In a game with this mod and the factory mod alone the wreck offers no study.
The player must order every study session, and no colonist ever goes back to the wreck by himself.
A colonist studies the wreck for a moment and the project opens; the study took no time that a player would notice.
leaves.lazy: A colonist studies the wreck for a moment and the project opens; the study took no time that a player would notice.

range.varies: Each ancient machine, grouped: a large factory machine and the two carried machines. Both studies: the wreck for the first project, the Kludged machine for the second. A wreck at home and a wreck studied where it was found. A game with this mod and the factory mod alone, and a game with Research Reinvented loaded (the small list holds it; its own study opportunities stay on top). A colonist who can research and one who cannot. A reload in the middle of a study.
range.left_out: How long a study takes and what a project costs: tuning data in Mod Settings. Research Reinvented's own rules (its field kit, its order for each session): that mod's. A wreck in its carried form: it is studied only while it stands. A machine destroyed in the middle of its study: the colony keeps the progress, because the base game keeps study by kind of thing; not judged.

sees.instrument: One wreck, one researcher and the clock, in a loaded game: jawa/research_availability for the first restoration project before any study (not startable, the studied-thing requirement unmet); the study turned on by its gizmo on the selected wreck (rimworld/list_selected_gizmos, rimworld/execute_gizmo); the researcher's job read while the clock advances (jawa/safe_advance); the wreck's inspect text read for its progress (jawa/inspect_string); then jawa/research_availability again. The same for the Kludged machine and the second project. A numeric read of study progress needs one generic bridge function that does not exist yet (read the game's study record for a kind of thing): a build item of the scene.
sees.start: A loaded game on the mod's small list (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/version/small_list.json), all five expansions, a quicktest map. No restoration project started or finished and no study recorded for the machine's kind (asserted). One colonist who can research, with no job. A powered research bench of the kind that the project needs.
sees.on: The machine's line on. Study switched on for the wreck. No development command on research or study.
sees.control: The cheapest other explanation is a project that would open anyway. In the same starting state with study never turned on, the clock advances the same length, a researcher works at the bench, and the project is still locked.
sees.reset: Reload the starting state; close the quicktest map.
sees.live_only_why: The study is a colonist's job on a building. The base game uses that study on items only, and nobody has seen it on a building in play (models.md, 'Study on a building').

leaves.experience: Colonists study the machine itself, and only that study opens the research for its next repair.

leaves.says: A player orders a repair on the machine, colonists bring the materials and work at it where it stands, and the machine stays in sight at its old level until the work is complete.

meant.intent: Reject if false: the first look at the built mod saw a repair as a pick from the build menu: a colonist took the wreck apart and then built a grey frame on empty ground. It read 'as a new build where the wreck stood, not a repair of the wreck'. A machine that took a journey to find must never be lost to a cancelled order.
meant.source: OWNER:1795755622961436106 ('slowly repaired through several levels'; 'considerable resources'); OWNER:1795749529567808948 ('repairing big machines in place, and that's excellent'); delegated: record decisions d_repair_is_made_on_the_machine (call A of turn 5, CONDUCTOR:1795770570858909459) and d_first_look_read reading 2.

figurative.stands_for: at the machine, with no workbench and no pick from the build menu. A machine at home and a machine still in its ruin are both repaired where they stand.
figurative.accept: A colony repairs a wreck that it found on its own map without moving it first.

figurative.stands_for: the machine is drawn, can be selected and is that machine during the whole repair. A mark on it may show that a repair is under way.
figurative.accept: During the repair the wreck carries a repair mark and lists the materials that are still missing, and it is still the wreck.

accept: The player selects a wreck whose study and research are done and orders the repair to Kludged on it. Colonists haul the materials to the wreck and work on it. The wreck is there the whole time. When the work is complete the Kludged machine stands in its place and faces the same way.
The player cancels a repair after part of the materials arrived. The wreck still stands, and the delivered materials lie beside it.
Something interrupts a repair for days. Afterwards colonists go on with the same repair.
A wreck whose research is not done shows the repair order as unavailable, and the order says what is missing.
A colony repairs a wreck that it found on its own map without moving it first.
reject: The player picks the next level from the build menu and places it over the wreck. A colonist takes the wreck apart and then builds a frame on empty ground.
The player cancels a repair, and the wreck is gone.
The machine changes level when the order is given, before any colonist has worked on it.
After a reload in the middle of a repair, the repair is forgotten and the delivered materials are lost.
leaves.lazy: none: the words name who orders, where the work is done and what stays in sight. The lazy build is the built mod (a build-menu pick over the wreck); it fails 'on the machine' and 'stays in sight'. No other build that does the three things and that he would refuse was found.

range.varies: Each ancient machine, grouped: a large factory machine in each of its four facings, and a carried machine. Both repairs: to Kludged and to Refurbished. The order given before and after the materials are in a stockpile. A cancel at three points: before any delivery, after part of the materials, during the work. A reload in the middle of a repair. A machine with no power. Two machines of one kind under repair at the same time.
range.left_out: What a repair costs and how long the work takes: tuning data in Mod Settings ('considerable resources' is his word; the amount is not a bar). A machine destroyed by fire or attack during a repair: it is destroyed like any building (rule R_destroyable). Which skill the work needs. A machine uninstalled during a repair: rule R_uninstall_cancels, read by the scene sc_uninstall_during_repair.

sees.instrument: One machine, one colonist and one order, in a loaded game: the repair order read and given on the selected machine (rimworld/list_selected_gizmos, rimworld/execute_gizmo); jawa/list_things for the machine's def at its cell at every step (the list must never be empty); the colonist's jobs read while the clock advances; the level read at the end. Then the same with a cancel at each of the three points, and once with a save and a reload during the work.
sees.start: A loaded game on the mod's small list (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/version/small_list.json), all five expansions, a quicktest map. A Wrecked machine installed at a known cell (asserted def and cell). Its first study complete and its first project finished (asserted by jawa/research_availability). The materials in a stockpile (asserted count). One free colonist who can do the work.
sees.on: The machine's line on. A test listener on the neutral level-changed signal (rule R_signal): the scene asserts that it fired once, with the machine, the old level and the new level.
sees.control: The cheapest other explanation is a level that changes without the repair. A second wreck of the same kind beside the first, with no order, is still Wrecked at the end. A third wreck whose project is not finished shows the order as unavailable.
sees.reset: Destroy the spawned things; close the quicktest map.
sees.live_only_why: The repair is an order, hauling and work by a colonist over time, with a cancel and a reload in the middle. The first look already showed that def data which reads well on paper plays as a build menu.

leaves.experience: A player orders a repair on the machine, colonists bring the materials and work at it where it stands, and the machine stays in sight at its old level until the work is complete.

leaves.says: A Wrecked machine does no work, a Kludged machine does a small part of the machine's work, a Refurbished machine does all of it, and no repaired machine does it as well as the Original.

meant.intent: Reject if false: the levels are what the repairs buy. His statement: 'wrecked (nonfunctional), Kludged (minimal), Refurbished (full functionality but slower than original)'. His ruling: 'There is nothing beyond or even equal to the original.' The value of a repaired machine is that the colony has it at all. In the built mod the power-cell wreck gives a faint current and the Refurbished smelter lacks one of the smelter's jobs.
meant.source: OWNER:1795755622961436106; OWNER:1795749411129133147; OWNER:1795749512608610645 (the battery that loses capacity and still works: read as the Kludged and Refurbished levels); OWNER:1795769070699312426 ('1: b.': plasteel is the recipe that the alloy forge's last repair brings); OWNER:1795755673273656447 (each machine's recipes and rates at each level are its onboarding); delegated: record decisions d_wrecked_gives_nothing, d_plasteel_with_last_repair (gravlite goes with plasteel: call C of turn 5, CONDUCTOR:1795770570858909459) and d_all_eighteen_shape call 8.

figurative.stands_for: what the machine is for: products for a factory machine, power for the power cell, a calmer mood nearby for the psychic emanator.
figurative.accept: A Kludged power cell lights a few lamps and a Refurbished one runs a workshop, and the base game's own power cell would give more than either.

figurative.stands_for: slower for a machine that makes goods; weaker for the power cell and the emanator. Whatever a player sets in Mod Settings, the order Wrecked, Kludged, Refurbished, Original holds.
figurative.accept: A player moves the Refurbished setting as high as it goes, and the Refurbished smelter is still slower than the Original.

figurative.stands_for: the machine's onboarding table names which of its products the Kludged level makes. A machine with one product makes that product slowly at the Kludged level.
figurative.accept: The Kludged alloy forge, in a game with this mod and the factory mod alone, makes obsidian and nothing else.

accept: A wrecked power cell joined to a power net gives no power, and a wrecked emanator calms nobody. A wreck may glow faintly, and that light does nothing.
A Kludged smelter smelts slag into steel and refuses the harder jobs. The Refurbished smelter takes every job that the factory mod's smelter takes, and each job takes longer than on the Original.
The Kludged alloy forge offers no plasteel. The Refurbished forge makes plasteel and gravlite.
A colony keeps a machine Kludged for the whole game and gets real use from it every day.
A player moves the Refurbished setting as high as it goes, and the Refurbished smelter is still slower than the Original.
reject: A wrecked power cell gives a faint current.
The Kludged machine does everything that the Refurbished one does, only slower, so the last repair buys nothing that a player would name.
The Refurbished smelter lacks one of the jobs of the factory mod's smelter.
With the level settings raised, a Refurbished machine matches the Original or beats it.
A Kludged machine makes one of the machine's products, and it is the one that a colony needs least, so a Kludged machine is of no use to anyone.
leaves.lazy: A Kludged machine makes one of the machine's products, and it is the one that a colony needs least, so a Kludged machine is of no use to anyone.

range.varies: Each of the 20 machines at each of its levels, grouped: machines that make goods by several processes (the smelter, the alloy forge and the like); machines with one product (the drill platform, the autofarmer, the fish farm); the power cell; the emanator. The level settings in Mod Settings at their lowest, shipped and highest values. With power and without. In the campaign's mod list the Kludged forge also makes durasteel, after the Armoury adds its recipe to the forge's levels (rule R_neighbour_names).
range.left_out: The numbers: how much slower, how much power, how strong the mood, how often a Kludged machine breaks down. They are tuning data and are kept as check C_level_numbers. Which products each Kludged machine makes: its onboarding table (rule R_onboarding), judged here only as 'a useful small part'. The Original as a thing that a colony reaches: no bar. Overclocking and the factory mod's boosters: as the onboarding table says for each level.

sees.instrument: A state read for every machine and level, and one production run for one machine of each group, in a loaded game. The read: the processes that the level offers (jawa/comp_read), its power (jawa/power_net) and, for the emanator, the thoughts of a colonist beside it (jawa/pawn_thoughts). The run: one product made at the Kludged level, at the Refurbished level and on an Original placed for comparison, with the ticks that each took. meetings.why: A machine has one level at a time, and only two things set it: placement (always Wrecked) and a completed repair (one step up). Carrying, study, a cancel and a reload read the level and never change it; taking the machine apart ends it. So no two bars ask for different levels of one machine at one moment. The offline walk C_repair_state_walk checks the same statement over every state and event.

The build menu holds the factory mod's parts and floor always, and a production machine only while its line is off. The two bars read the same menu in the two states of one switch, so they cannot disagree. The floor must stay (R_ground), or a carried-home wreck could never be repaired; R_parts_stay keeps it.

Three kinds of thing pass through the game's hand-outs and each has one rule: a working machine is never handed out while its line is on; a wreck is placed only by this mod's own lists; a component lies only in ruin rooms. A line that is off gives back the base game's hand-out of that machine and stops the placement of its wrecks. None of the three rules reads another's list.

The settings are of three kinds that do not overlap: one on/off line for each machine, the tuning numbers (levels, costs, placement), and the riders' switches as built. The kernel clamps the level numbers so that no value breaks the order of the levels. Every setting is re-derived from the shipped defs when it is applied, so off and on again returns the shipped state; the sweep of switch_gives_machine_back reads that.

A restoration project opens a repair order and never a build-menu entry, so finishing every project cannot break only_by_repair. Each project is locked by one study and unlocks one repair; the forge has no third project (R_forge). The 20 machines bring 40 projects: they sit on one research tab of their own so that they do not crowd the base game's tabs (plan.md, load).

Wrecks and components come from one placement list with separate weights, so a ruin can hold both and the whole run can start from one generated ruin. Cold Storage already adds a wrecked locker to Odyssey's ruin rooms by the same route with no C# (record decision d_feasible_wreck_placement). The flood and the desert are the two ends of the weights; the whole bar rejects both, and the weights are tuning data.

A wreck is always movable and may stand on any firm ground, so it can always come home. A working level needs the donor's ground, so the repair order checks the ground and says what is missing; a colony lays factory floor at the place where it installs the wreck. An uninstall during a repair is a cancel. Whether floor can be laid under a wreck that already stands is not measured; if it cannot, the colony carries the wreck onto floor, which the same rules allow.

The base game's study has been read in source and never seen on a building in play. Not known: whether a researcher takes the study job on a building by himself, whether the research screen names the unstudied machine, and what a player sees when Research Reinvented's study of the same machine is on top.

One order on the machine has one list of needs: the finished project, the ground, the materials and, for the last repair, the component. The order is unavailable with a reason for each missing need, so the bars that add a need (the component, the ground) all show through the same place. A cancel, an uninstall and a reload act on the one repair record of the machine.
The only event that changes a level after placement is a completed repair, so the signal has one place to fire. The repair scene's listener counts it.

The forge's onboarding row follows the one rule of every row, with his card as its fixed point: plasteel (and gravlite, which is made from plasteel) at Refurbished only. The Kludged forge keeps a useful part in the campaign through the Armoury's durasteel, which lands in the same change as the forge's onboarding (R_neighbour_names). With this mod and the factory mod alone the Kludged forge makes obsidian only; the page of turn 5 told him so.

A wreck joins no net (R_wreck_inert), so it gives and takes nothing (levels_of_function) and shows no power mark; a line may still draw to it by its tag (wrecks_join_lines). The marks on a repaired level come from its real power state, which the picture bar reads beside the capture.

The table is the one place where a machine's levels are written; the bar reads the game and the offline check C_onboarding_table_offline reads the table against the donor's defs. Whether a level can be moved is a field of the same row.

The component has one way in (a ruin room) and one way out (a last repair). Taking any machine apart gives none, so a colony cannot turn found wrecks into components. Neighbours also charge it (Cold Storage, the Cuisine mod's stasis), so each component is a choice, and a machine that stays Kludged is normal play.
Three looks cover the levels that a colony can hold at one time; the fourth level shares the third's picture and is told apart by name. The art judge reads each new picture against the canon library.

The text that must agree with the picture (the inspect text and the order reasons) is part of the text that the offline read searches for setting words and for the old level name. The bars and the rule read the same strings for three different faults, and one change of a string can repair all three.

src/RimMandrake/FlowWorks/selftest_wrecked_links_draw_in.py reads the shipped XML and holds both halves today: a tagged wreck draws lines in, and a tagged wreck holds no comp that could join a net. It is green on the built smelter wreck; it must read all 20 wrecks after their onboarding.

rules.rule: A machine enters this mod by an onboarding table that is written by hand in 0.1.0: its levels, what each level makes and how fast, its two restoration projects, what each repair costs, whether its Kludged level can be moved, and its pictures. One rule binds every table: Kludged is a useful small part of the machine's work, and Refurbished is all of it and slower than the Original. The build takes the smelter first and then the machines in the order in which the campaign needs them.

Each machine has two restoration projects. Study of the wreck opens the first, and study of the Kludged machine opens the second. A project is the colony's knowledge: a second machine of the same kind needs no new study and no new research.

Study is carried by the base game's own study of a thing (the comp that unlocks research after analysis, and a project's list of things that must be analysed), put on a building. It needs no other mod and no item. With Research Reinvented loaded, that mod's study opportunities at the machine stay on top. A machine is studied only while it stands, not in its carried form.

Where wrecks and Ancient Components lie is data: a weighted list for ruin rooms and a rare single wreck for ordinary new maps. A layer above can change the list without this mod knowing. Every machine that is placed is at the Wrecked level. The placement reads no biome; it reads whether a ruin room or open ground exists. A machine whose line is off is not placed.
Every wreck has a carried form and weighs what the donor machine weighs. Who may lift a wreck is data on the machine; as shipped, any colonist may. This mod requires no hauler mod and names none.

Whether a Kludged or a Refurbished machine can be moved is a field of its onboarding table. As built: the Kludged smelter cannot be moved, the Refurbished smelter can, and the carried machines can at every level.
An order to uninstall a machine that is under repair cancels the repair first, as a cancel by the player does: the delivered materials are given back, and the machine is carried at its old level.

A wreck stands on any ground that carries a heavy building. A working level needs the ground that the donor machine needs: for the factory machines, the factory mod's own floor. A repair order on a wreck that stands on other ground is unavailable and says so. The factory floor stays in the build menu behind the factory mod's own research, like the other parts.
A machine of this mod at any level can be attacked, burnt and taken apart like any building. Taking one apart gives ordinary scrap and never an Ancient Component.

The factory mod's parts that do not make goods stay researched and built as that mod has them: the conveyors, the underground conveyor ends, the hopper, the booster, the heatsink and the factory floor. The base game's electric smelter is not touched. A machine that stands in an older save is not changed.

Two rules in the mod's folder are outside its promise and work as built until they move: the one salvage rule (to shared code with its own home) and the distillation machine (its working form to FlowWorks). No bar of 0.1.0 judges what they do; their settings stay as built. The alloy forge's early research step and its two settings end when the forge is onboarded.
When a machine changes level, the mod raises one neutral signal that carries the machine, the old level and the new level. The mod names no listener and knows none.
A Refurbished machine may use the Original's picture. Each Wrecked and each Kludged level has a picture of its own; a shade of another level's picture is not a picture of its own.

On the alloy forge, plasteel and gravlite are processes of the Refurbished level only, and no research project of their own locks them. Durasteel stays the Armoury's recipe, which the Armoury adds to the forge's Kludged and Refurbished levels.

A name that a neighbour mod reads (a def name, a class, a research project) changes only together with that neighbour's file, in one landing. The Armoury's forge recipes and ResearchRetag's tab patch are the two known cases of 0.1.0.

A player reads four level names and no others: Wrecked, Kludged, Refurbished and Original. No label, description, order or settings line calls a level Repaired. A defName that keeps the old word is build detail, changed only under R_neighbour_names.
A Wrecked def holds no comp that joins a power net or a pipe net. It carries only the draw-in tags that make lines draw to it.
